name: Shabaki
world_status: accessible description is silent on stress

sources.citation: Karim, Shuan Osman & Saloumeh Gholami (eds.). 2024. Gorani in its Historical and Linguistic Context. Berlin/Boston: De Gruyter Mouton (open access, CC BY-NC-ND; via OAPEN).
sources.access_detail: a copy the project holds (available on request)
sources.note: Discusses Shabaki only for morphology/classification (ch. 1 pp. 7-8, 28-29; ch. 3 p. 98); says 'So little is known about Shabaki..' and cites Mahmoudveysi & Bailey (in prep.) 'The Gūrānī varieties in and around Mosul known as Šabakī/Baǰaɫānī'. Stress remarks in the volume concern Hawrami varieties (gender by stressed/unstressed final vowel), not Shabaki.

sources.citation: Schiering, René & Harry van der Hulst. 2010. Word accent systems in the languages of Asia. In van der Hulst, Goedemans & van Zanten (eds.), A Survey of Word Accentual Patterns in the Languages of the World, 509-599. Berlin: De Gruyter Mouton.
sources.access_detail: a copy the project holds (available on request); access check: publisher record (DOI); no open copy and no library e-access found (also a publisher record (DOI), probably paywalled)
sources.note: 'Shabak' appears only in the Zaza-Gorani line of the genealogical listing (p. 564); no StressTyp extract or accent statement for Shabak/Shabaki (Wikipedia cites this book only for classification).

sources.citation: Sultan, Abbas H. J. 2016. An account of epistemic modality in Shabaki. Kufa Journal of Arts 1(26): 9-24. DOI 10.36317/kaj/2015/v1.i26.6143.
sources.access_detail: a copy the project holds (available on request)
sources.note: Only a transcription key in the endnotes (segment values); no mention of stress.

sources.citation: Leezenberg, Michiel. 1994. The Shabak and the Kakais: Dynamics of Ethnicity in Iraqi Kurdistan. ILLC Technical Notes X-1994-07, University of Amsterdam.
sources.access_detail: a copy the project holds (available on request)
sources.note: Linguistic appendix (pp. 15-17) gives Shabaki (Qahrawa) numerals, pronouns and verb paradigms and a few phonetic remarks (*hw- > w-, Arbil-Kurdish affrication among Sarli speakers); nothing on stress (scanned read in full).

sources.citation: Leezenberg, Michiel. 1993. Gorani Influence on Central Kurdish: Substratum or Prestige Borrowing? ILLC Prepublication X-1993-03, University of Amsterdam.
sources.access_detail: a copy the project holds (available on request)
sources.note: Nothing on word stress (scanned a full-text search for stress/accent: 'stress' only in non-linguistic senses).

sources.citation: MacKenzie, D. N. 1956. Bājalānī. Bulletin of the School of Oriental and African Studies 18(3): 418-435. (Informant from Arpachi near Mosul who called his own tongue 'Šabakī'; treated by Karim & Gholami 2024 as the sketch of Shabaki/Bajalani.)
sources.access_detail: a copy the project holds (available on request); access check: online with a university library login
sources.note: Nothing. Grammatical notes (nouns, pronouns, verb paradigms), sentences and a glossary; transcription carries macrons only, no stress marks (pages viewed as images); no statement on stress or accent anywhere in pp. 418-435.

sources.citation: MacKenzie, D. N. 2002. Gurāni. Encyclopaedia Iranica XI/4: 401-403; and MacKenzie 1988. Bājalān. Encyclopaedia Iranica III.

sources.note: Hadank's treatment of Mann's Bajalani material from Xorsabad (Khorsabad, in the Shabak area east of Mosul) and Zohab; Hadank routinely includes a 'Betonung' (stress) paragraph, so this is the likeliest existing printed stress remark for Mosul-area Gorani. US public domain since 2026 but no open scan located.
